key_insight: A two-level machine-learning pipeline can map free-energy landscapes of complex hybrid perovskite alloys, revealing where thermodynamically stable compositions exist and where they do not.
engineering_relevance: The results help narrow design targets for more stable perovskite solar absorbers, especially by showing that Sn-based alloys have a smaller viable composition window than Pb-based ones.
method: Graph neural network interatomic potentials were trained on DFT data to rapidly relax alloy structures.
Secondary ML models predicted energies directly from unrelaxed structures, reducing the cost of exploring quaternary composition space.
The workflow captured alloy disorder and FA molecular orientations in free-energy calculations.
evidence_signal: The approach enabled free-energy landscape calculations across compositions and phases for both (Cs/FA)Pb(Br/I)3 and (Cs/FA)Sn(Br/I)3, distinguishing their stability regions.
watch_item: The stability predictions rely on ML models trained to DFT data, so transferability outside the sampled chemistry and composition space may be limited.
paper_title: Charting the thermodynamic stability of hybrid perovskite alloys with machine learning
